topic: Google Cloud Professional Data Engineer certification exam preparation - designing, building, operationalizing, securing, and monitoring data processing systems and ML-ready pipelines on Google Cloud (BigQuery, BigQuery ML, Dataflow, Dataproc, Pub/Sub, Cloud Composer, Vertex AI)
cert_name: Google Cloud Certified - Professional Data Engineer
exam_format: Approximately 50-60 questions, 120 minutes, delivered online-proctored or at a test center. Multiple choice (single answer) and multiple select, in a NON-adaptive, heavily scenario-based format. Google uses scaled scoring and does NOT publish an official passing percentage - present pass thresholds as unpublished. The certification is valid for two years. Exam fee is approximately USD 200 (plus tax where applicable) and varies by region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current Google Cloud pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'; every item is a real-world scenario asking which Google Cloud service or design fits - NOT term definitions
audience: Data engineers, ETL/data-pipeline developers, analytics engineers, and ML/data platform practitioners who build and operate data systems on Google Cloud. Google recommends 3+ years of industry experience including 1+ year designing and managing solutions on Google Cloud. Strong SQL and general data-engineering fundamentals are assumed. A natural companion to the Google Professional Machine Learning Engineer and Associate Cloud Engineer courses already in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Designing data processing systems
domains.notes: Choosing the right storage and processing architecture for a described requirement: relational vs analytical vs NoSQL (Cloud SQL, BigQuery, Bigtable, Spanner, Firestore), and batch vs streaming pipelines. Designing for reliability, scalability, cost, and latency; schema and data-modeling choices (partitioning, clustering, denormalization in BigQuery); migration and hybrid designs; selecting Dataflow vs Dataproc vs Data Fusion vs Dataform for a transformation; designing for data governance, lineage, and mesh. The recurring skill is matching a business/technical scenario to the correct GCP data service and pattern.

domains.name: Ingesting and processing the data
domains.notes: The heaviest domain. Building pipelines: streaming ingestion with Pub/Sub and Dataflow (Apache Beam) - windowing, watermarks, late data, exactly-once; batch ingestion and ETL/ELT; Dataproc (Spark/Hadoop) for lift-and-shift and heavy transforms; Datastream for CDC; Data Fusion and Dataform for managed/SQL transforms; orchestration with Cloud Composer (Airflow). Handling schema drift, error/dead-letter handling, idempotency, and throughput/cost tuning. Choosing the right ingestion + processing tool for a described data source, volume, and latency.

domains.name: Storing the data
domains.notes: Selecting and optimizing storage: BigQuery (partitioning, clustering, materialized views, slots vs on-demand, storage/compute separation), Bigtable (row-key design, hotspotting), Cloud Storage (classes, lifecycle), Spanner and Cloud SQL for transactional needs. Data lifecycle, retention, and cost optimization; time-travel and snapshots; choosing the correct store for access patterns, scale, and consistency. Matching a described query/access pattern to the optimal storage service and layout.

domains.name: Preparing and using data for analysis and ML
domains.notes: Making data useful and ML-ready: BigQuery for analytics; BigQuery ML for in-warehouse models; feature engineering and the handoff to Vertex AI (training, pipelines, feature store, model deployment) and MLOps basics (operationalizing and automating models). Data visualization and BI with Looker / Looker Studio; sharing datasets (Analytics Hub). Choosing BigQuery ML vs Vertex AI for a described modeling need, and preparing data so models and dashboards are reliable and reproducible.

domains.name: Maintaining and automating data workloads; security and compliance
domains.notes: Operating and securing pipelines in production: automating and scheduling workloads (Composer, scheduled queries), monitoring and alerting (Cloud Monitoring/Logging), troubleshooting and optimizing running pipelines, and ensuring quality (testing, data validation, SLAs, disaster recovery). Security and compliance: IAM roles and least privilege, CMEK/encryption, VPC Service Controls, column/row-level security and data masking in BigQuery, DLP for sensitive data, and regulatory considerations (residency, retention). Choosing the correct operational or security control for a described production scenario.

extra_guidance: Google Cloud Professional Data Engineer (PDE) is one of the most respected and highest-paying cloud data credentials, and it is HEAVILY scenario-based - the real skill the exam tests is 'given this requirement, which Google Cloud service and design is best,' NOT memorizing definitions. Make every chapter decision-oriented and use EXACT current Google Cloud product names: BigQuery, BigQuery ML, Dataflow (Apache Beam), Dataproc, Pub/Sub, Data Fusion, Dataform, Datastream, Cloud Composer (Airflow), Cloud Storage, Bigtable, Spanner, Cloud SQL, Vertex AI (training, pipelines, feature store), Looker / Looker Studio, Analytics Hub, Dataplex, and Cloud DLP - with a one-line note that Google's data/AI product names evolve, so verify against current docs. The AI/ML angle is real and testable: cover BigQuery ML for in-warehouse models and Vertex AI for training/serving/MLOps, and the decision of BQML vs Vertex AI. The five domain names and weights above reflect Google's current exam-guide sections; present the percentages as APPROXIMATE editorial estimates aligned to the guide (Google's guide gives ranges, not fixed splits) and say so where weights appear. Labs are READ-AND-UNDERSTAND design walkthroughs (design a streaming pipeline with Pub/Sub + Dataflow, choose a BigQuery partitioning/clustering scheme, design a Bigtable row key, wire an Airflow DAG in Composer, build a BigQuery ML model, set column-level security) - the exam is about judgment, not console clicks; make that explicit. Practice questions MUST be scenario-style: batch vs streaming, Dataflow vs Dataproc, BigQuery vs Bigtable vs Spanner, on-demand vs slots, BQML vs Vertex AI, IAM/VPC-SC/CMEK choices, and cost/latency trade-offs. Cover the classic traps: partitioning vs clustering, exactly-once vs at-least-once, hotspotting in Bigtable, denormalization in BigQuery, when to use materialized views. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 200, varies by region) and note the two-year validity; advise verifying current Google Cloud pricing and the latest exam guide. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 120-minute, scenario-pacing time-management strategy. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (AWS/Azure/NVIDIA) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
